title: Evaluating Robustness of Dialogue Summarization Models in the Presence of Naturally Occurring Variations

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting synthetic utterances requesting repetition and paraphrased repeated responses into dialogues to test if models inappropriately consider repeated information to be more significant.
Adding synthetic greeting remarks at the beginning of dialogues to examine if the model exhibits a preference for extracting summary information from the first utterance.
Adding synthetic closing remarks at the end of dialogues to investigate if the model inappropriately prefers to include information from the last utterance.

Splitting and combining consecutive utterances to simulate variations in message length, evaluating if the model prefers to include long utterances over shorter ones even when short ones contain salient information.

Applying lexical and morphosyntactic transformation rules to convert standard English utterances into synthetic African American Vernacular English (AAVE) and evaluating the summarization model's performance drop.
